questions.stem: When magnesium reacts with oxygen, magnesium atoms lose 2 electrons. What charge does the magnesium ion have?
questions.explanation: When magnesium loses 2 electrons, it has 12 protons (+12) but only 10 electrons (-10). The overall charge is +12 + (-10) = +2, giving Mg²⁺. Losing electrons always produces positive ions (cations) because there are now more protons than electrons.

questions.stem: Calcium (Group 2) reacts with fluorine (Group 7). What is the formula of the compound formed?
questions.explanation: Calcium has 2 outer electrons and forms Ca²⁺. Each fluorine atom needs 1 electron and forms F⁻. To balance the charges, one Ca²⁺ ion needs two F⁻ ions: (2+) + 2(1-) = 0. The formula is CaF₂. A common error is to write CaF, forgetting that two fluoride ions are needed to balance the 2+ charge.

questions.stem: In ionic bonding, what happens to the electrons?

options.text: Electrons are transferred from metal atoms to non-metal atoms
Electrons are destroyed during the reaction
Electrons become delocalised and move freely

questions.explanation: In ionic bonding, electrons are transferred from metal atoms (which lose electrons to form positive ions) to non-metal atoms (which gain electrons to form negative ions). The electrons are not shared (that's covalent), not destroyed (conservation of charge), and not delocalised (that's metallic bonding).

questions.stem: A sodium atom (2, 8, 1) forms an ionic bond with a chlorine atom (2, 8, 7). What are the electronic structures of the ions formed?
questions.explanation: Sodium loses its one outer electron (from the third shell), giving Na⁺ the electronic structure 2, 8 (same as neon). Chlorine gains this electron, giving Cl⁻ the electronic structure 2, 8, 8 (same as argon). Both ions now have full outer shells, which is a stable noble gas configuration.

questions.stem: Why do ionic compounds form between metals and non-metals rather than between two metals?

options.text: Metals are too heavy to bond with each other
Metals tend to lose electrons, so they need non-metals which tend to gain electrons
Non-metals are always more reactive than metals
Metals can only form covalent bonds with each other

questions.explanation: Ionic bonding requires one atom to lose electrons and another to gain them. Metals have few outer electrons and lose them readily, while non-metals need a few more electrons to fill their outer shell and gain them readily. Two metals would both try to lose electrons with nothing to gain them, so ionic bonding cannot occur between two metals.
